Comment: Overt ABS markers: particles ye/ti for NPs, Class I pronouns (ako, ka, ya, hila) for persons (Chart 1, p.1; Chart 2, p.3).
Class I (ABS): ako (1sg); Class II (ERG): ko. Clear ABS/ERG distinction on 1st person pronouns.
Class I (ABS): ka (2sg); Class II (ERG): mo. Clear ABS/ERG distinction.
Class I (ABS): ya (3sg), hila (3pl); Class II (ERG): na (3sg), la (3pl). Clear ABS/ERG distinction.
ABS particle ye/ti vs. ERG particle nin/ne for full NPs; consistent ERG alignment on full NPs.
ERG alignment in progressive/imperfective aspect (aN- prefix); agent takes Class II (ERG).
ERG alignment in perfective aspect (-in- infix); agent takes Class II (ERG).
Past events (na- prefix) maintain ERG alignment.
Non-past/future (m- prefix) clauses maintain ERG alignment.
Indicative declaratives consistently show ERG alignment.
Imperatives and other non-indicative forms maintain ERG alignment.
Completed/realis clauses maintain ERG alignment.
Irrealis (future, imperative, purpose) maintains ERG alignment.
Agentive A (volitional actors) takes Class II (ERG) pronouns or ERG particle nin.
Source does not discuss non-agentive/experiencer A; insufficient data to determine.
In Philippine-type system, topical argument is always in ABS; A is always non-topical and ERG. GB409_16=0 is the canonical pattern.
Non-topical A takes nin/Class II (ERG) consistently in all transitive examples.
All animate A in examples take ERG case.
No examples of inanimate A in this source; insufficient data.
Main clauses consistently show ERG alignment.
Subordinate clauses maintain ERG alignment (p.6, 19).
Personal demonstrative pronouns never take ERG because their inherent definiteness requires them to be the absolutive argument (§1.3.1, p.6). Definiteness-based conditioning of ERG.
Chart 1 (p.1) labels nin as 'ERG/GEN'; Class II pronouns used for both agent (ERG) and possessive (GEN) functions (pp.9-10).
Instrumental adverbs are case-marked with nin (the ERG/GEN marker): antoyhoken lan etak 'they are stabbing with machete' where etak (machete) = instrument marked with nin (§3.2.4, p.23).
